target.title: fix: screen and camera capture continue after cancellation
target.body:
Related: #357

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cancelled or timed-out screen and camera requests could continue capturing, and queued camera work could begin after its caller had already stopped waiting.

## Why This Change Was Made

This revisits the cancellation work attempted in closed PR #403 on top of the bounded concurrent dispatch architecture merged in #426. Unlike #403, this change preserves #426's receive-loop and eight-invoke concurrency model, keeps cancellation tokens outside serializable request DTOs, supports MCP `notifications/cancelled`, and propagates cancellation through consent/countdown and native capture cleanup. It intentionally does not add transport deadline policy.

Invocation completion is the linearization point: once capability execution returns and commits completion, later cancellation is too late. MCP duplicate JSON-RPC IDs fail safe when cancellation is ambiguous rather than allowing one local client to cancel another.

## User Impact

Cancelled screen recordings, camera clips, snapshots, consent waits, countdowns, and queued camera requests now stop cooperatively instead of continuing after the caller leaves. Gateway and local MCP callers receive a stable `cancelled` outcome when cancellation wins.

## Evidence

- Added focused coverage for gateway request/event cancellation, MCP cancellation and registration races, numeric/string IDs, completion races, capability token propagation, and queued camera admission.
- Raw MCP proof on an isolated current-head tray run discovered `camera.clip`, started `notifications/cancelled` before registration, received HTTP 204, and observed the matching call return `isError: true` with `cancelled`.
- Hanselman dual-model review of the integrated uncommitted change found no critical, high, medium, or consensus issues; the final low-severity diagnostics findings were addressed before commit.

- Evidence after fix: `CameraClipDiscovered=True`, cancellation HTTP status `204`, call ID `proof-window`, `IsError=True`, result text `cancelled`.

target.title: improve(setup): keep WSL operations inside the app-owned directory
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where developers running the standalone SetupEngine with a custom WSL distro name could cause cleanup or installation paths to resolve outside `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenClawTray\wsl`. Because cleanup recursively deletes the resolved path, a traversal value such as `..\..` could target an unintended directory.

No known user incident prompted this change. The packaged application supplies its fixed distro name after config/environment loading, so the exposed path is the repository/developer SetupEngine flow.

## Why This Change Was Made

Setup now derives every WSL distro install path through one policy that validates the distro name, canonicalizes the path, requires it to be an immediate child of the app-owned `wsl` root, and rejects reparse points at the trusted local-data root or WSL root. Recursive cleanup revalidates ownership before every retry, and rollback unregisters the name-based distro before attempting guarded filesystem cleanup.

The remaining same-user check-to-use filesystem race is accepted as a non-goal: additional checks can narrow it, but fully atomic deletion or `wsl --install` would require handle-based operating-system support that these APIs do not expose.

## User Impact

Developers invoking SetupEngine directly now receive a terminal validation error before WSL commands or recursive cleanup run when a distro name or install path is unsafe. Shipped/default distro names continue to work unchanged; packaged application users should see no behavioral difference.

## Evidence

The SetupEngine tests exercise real Windows junctions and verify that traversal values are rejected before commands run, paths outside the expected immediate child are never deleted, reparse-point ancestors are rejected, and a parent swapped to a junction during retry backoff is detected before the next recursive-delete attempt. The redirected sentinel file remains intact.

Three independent dual-model review passes found no blocking correctness issue. The only recurring observation was the documented same-user check-to-use limitation.

- `dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore` — 2,863 passed, 31 skipped, 0 failed

- PR head or commit tested: `e2c7889b`
- Exact steps or command run: full validation commands listed above; focused policy/deletion tests also run with `--filter "FullyQualifiedName~DistroInstallPathPolicy|FullyQualifiedName~DeleteDistroDirectory"`
- Evidence after fix: traversal, outside-target, junction-ancestor, and retry-time junction-swap tests all passed against real temporary filesystem paths

This reduces the execution/data risk; it does not add a new command or expand access. A same-user process can still theoretically race a filesystem check, which is documented as an accepted limitation.

target.title: fix: setup fails closed for invalid configuration arguments
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where users running SetupEngine with an invalid explicit configuration argument could silently load bundled defaults and start setup with settings they did not request. This includes missing option values, paths that do not exist, unreadable or malformed files, and semantically empty JSON. For example, with `--config --headless`, the old parser treated `--headless` as the config filename. Because that file did not exist, SetupEngine silently loaded `default-config.json` instead, while separately recognizing `--headless` as an active flag. The result was an unattended setup run using bundled settings rather than the caller's intended configuration. Since those defaults enable `CleanBeforeRun`, a simple malformed command could unregister the existing app-owned WSL distro and remove its setup-managed gateway state before rebuilding it. A typo in an explicit config path had the same fallback behavior. ## Why This Change Was Made SetupEngine now validates every value-taking option before loading configuration or starting setup. Explicit configuration failures return a controlled error and never fall back to bundled defaults; bundled defaults remain available only when `--config` is omitted. ## User Impact Operators and automation now receive an immediate error for invalid setup arguments instead of risking an unintended setup run or cleanup using bundled defaults. Existing valid invocations remain unchanged. ## Evidence - Added focused parser coverage for all nine value-taking options, including missing, blank, whitespace-only, flag-valued, and duplicate arguments. - Added end-to-end `Program.Main` coverage for missing, malformed, empty, whitespace-only, JSON `null`, unreadable, invalid-path, and valid explicit configurations. - Final dual-model Hanselman review found no correctness or security defects. ### Screenshots 1. Motivating malformed command 2. Nonexistent explicit config 3. Valid explicit config dry run ## Change Type - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Docs or instructions - [x] Tests or validation - [x] Security hardening - [ ] Chore or infrastructure ## Scope - [ ] Tray or WinUI UX - [ ] Windows node capability - [ ] Local MCP or `winnode` - [ ] Gateway, connection, or pairing - [x] Setup or onboarding - [x] Permissions, privacy, or security - [x] Tests, CI, or docs ## Validation - `.\build.ps1` — passed - `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests\OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests.csproj --no-restore` — 488 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped - `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Shared.Tests\OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore` — 2,863 passed, 0 failed, 31 conditionally skipped - `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore` — 1,717 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped ## Real Behavior Proof - Environment tested: Windows ARM64, .NET SDK 10.0.301 - PR head or commit tested: `11fd4808` - Exact steps or command run: focused `ProgramArgumentTests` through `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests\OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests.csproj --no-restore` - Evidence after fix: invalid explicit configuration cases return exit code 2 before setup; valid explicit configuration with `--dry-run` returns exit code 0 - Observed result: all 488 SetupEngine tests passed, including every added fail-closed regression case - Screenshot or artifact links verified? (`Yes`/`No`/`N/A`): N/A - Not verified or blocked: None ## Security Impact - New permissions or capabilities? (`Yes`/`No`): No - Secrets or tokens handling changed? (`Yes`/`No`): No - New or changed network calls? (`Yes`/`No`): No - Command or tool execution surface changed? (`Yes`/`No`): No - Data access scope changed? (`Yes`/`No`): No - If any answer is `Yes`, explain the risk and mitigation: N/A ## Compatibility and Migration - Backward compatible?
